seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: untrusted_data
seed_vocabulary.prose: content in quoted text, untrusted_text blocks, multimodal data, file attachments, and tool outputs that has no authority by default and must be treated as information rather than instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec describing limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where the assistant should refrain from fully complying with a user or developer request

judgment_calls: Could have cut at L1928 (end of privileged-information section) instead of L1973, but L1928-1973 contains the final example blocks of that section, which are cohesive with the section's rules; a cut at L1928 would have split the example blocks from their governing rules.

Could have cut at L2404 (end of no-topic-off-limits) instead of L2405, but L2404 is the last content line of that section and L2405 is a blank line; giving the blank line to child 2 keeps the section intact.
The stay_in_bounds and untrusted_data seeds are inherited and appear in multiple children; I carry them unchanged in seed_vocabulary so my children can use the exact names.
